items.title: 'They got it all wrong': The miscalculation the US and Israel made over Iran
items.description: Donald Trump is deploying thousands of marines and extra battleships to the Middle East, while also claiming to be close to a deal with Iran to end the war. So is he set to wind down his war with Iran or is he thinking of escalating?

items.title: Israel warns attacks on Iran will expand as Trump delays Strait of Hormuz deadline
items.description: Israel has warned it will expand its attacks on Iran as Tehran kept firing missiles at Israel and Gulf nations.

items.title: The oil crisis is meeting a military stockpile crisis
items.description: While markets struggle to price a sudden collapse in oil supply military analysts are sounding the alarm on the rate countries are burning through weapons stockpiles.

items.title: Northern WA picks up the pieces in the wake of Cyclone Narelle
items.description: Tropical Cyclone Narelle remains at category-two cyclone strength, as it continues to travel across the Gascoyne and Midwest.

items.title: When the Iran war ends, Australia's involvement could start
items.description: The federal government is turning its mind to what Australian support in the Middle East might look like after a ceasefire.

items.title: Is government intervention keeping LNG exporters on their 'best behaviour'?
items.description: With war in the Middle East throwing energy markets into chaos, Australian gas prices are strikingly subdued. Experts say looming intervention by Canberra may explain why.

items.title: TGA not 'sitting on our hands', defends handling of sunscreen scandal
items.description: In his first interview since the sunscreen controversy erupted almost 10 months ago, the Therapeutic Goods Administration head says he hopes the proposed shake-up of regulations will restore consumer confidence.

items.title: Customers hit with 'deceptive' fees after booking online travel
items.description: As holiday-makers gear up for Easter, online travel site Guest Reservations is accused of fleecing customers using hidden fees and charges with advocates calling on government and the regulator to step in.

items.title: Telstra outage in remote NT community impacting Triple Zero access
items.description: Residents in the remote NT community of Kintore have had difficulty making Triple Zero calls during a six-day Telstra outage, which has also caused issues buying fuel.

items.title: As Pakistan emerges as a US-Iran broker, it draws on relationships few others have
items.description: Pakistan is positioning itself at the centre of a war it is uniquely placed to influence and cannot afford to ignore, writes Meghna Bali.

items.title: Savannah Guthrie to return to Today show after mother's disappearance
items.description: Savannah Guthrie is scheduled to return to her job as a co-anchor of NBC's Today show on April 6, more than two months after her 84-year-old mother's unresolved abduction.

items.title: Man interviewed on suspicion of sex trafficking in Mohamed Al-Fayed investigation
items.description: Former Harrods boss Mohamed Al-Fayed, who died in 2023, has been accused of rape, sexual assault, sexual exploitation and human trafficking on a large scale.

items.title: Ukraine and Saudi Arabia sign 'mutually beneficial' air defence deal
items.description: The deal comes at a crucial time for Kyiv, as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said weapons for Ukraine could be diverted to the Iran war

items.title: 'There will be tax reform' but treasurer says no decision yet on capital gains
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers commits to tax reform in his upcoming budget, but adds that no decision has yet been taken as to whether capital gains tax will be part of those changes.

items.title: The nine books we couldn't put down in March
items.description: Wondering what to read next? Gothic crime fiction, a cult Japanese bestseller and a fantastical twist on the Blitz are among our critics' latest recommendations.

items.title: Our critics can't stop listening to these 10 albums from March
items.description: The year might've kicked off with a flood of great records, but March is when things really snap into gear.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: This week we're testing your knowledge of 80s punk rock, Harry Potter spoilers and that internet dress
items.description: Every question has only two options: one is right and the other is wrong. You have an even chance of guessing correctly each time.

items.title: Broncos claim pressure-relieving victory over Dolphins, ending tough week on a high
items.description: The Broncos overpowered the Dolphins 26-22 in the Battle of Brisbane, after Wests Tigers stunned ladder leaders New Zealand Warriors in Auckland.

items.title: AFL players to lose insurance coverage for brain injuries
items.description: More than 500 AFL players will soon no longer be covered by insurance for brain injuries in their superannuation after Zurich Insurance moved to cut their ability to claim for concussion and head trauma.

items.title: Magpies confirm 'hamstring awareness' for Moore after win over Giants
items.description: Collingwood is expecting to be without its skipper Darcy Moore and his predecessor Scott Pendlebury next week against Brisbane after the pair were hobbled during the win over GWS.

items.title: 'Forget it': NSW beachgoers urged to cancel plans amid hazardous weather
items.description: New South Wales beaches will be too dangerous to visit this weekend, with authorities issuing a warning to rock fishers, swimmers and boaters to stay away from the coastline.

items.title: Teenagers brandish knives, hammer at Canberra shopping centre
items.description: Police say they were called to the Canberra Centre about 6:20pm on Friday after reports that a group of young people were involved in a disturbance, brandishing knives and a hammer.

items.title: Socceroos snatch late win as teen debutant impresses heading into World Cup
items.description: Jordy Bos hits the back of the net as the Socceroos leave it late against Cameroon in Sydney with 18-year-old Lucas Herrington impressing on debut.

items.title: New Spirit of Tasmania ferry to be used as Dark Mofo floating art gallery
items.description: The new spirit of Tasmania ferries might not be available for journeys across the Bass Strait yet — but this winter, one of them will take on a new role as an art gallery, during Hobart's Dark Mofo festival.

items.title: The 'crown jewels' of the Iranian nuclear program and why the US wants them
items.description: A move from Israel or the United States to find and secure Iran's enriched uranium stockpile would be dangerous, but experts say it is one of the only ways to end the war and prevent it from returning.
